cards.locator: Section 1.3.1 (ETV6-Associated Thrombocytopenia and Predisposition to Leukemia — Overview)

cards.interpretation: Germline ETV6 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants confer an increased lifetime risk of hematologic malignancy, including CMML, MDS, AML, and a prominent risk of lymphoid leukemia.

cards.interpretation: CEBPA-associated familial AML is defined by a germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic CEBPA variant in a person with AML and/or in a family with more than one member affected by AML.
cards.locator: Section 2.1.1 (Overview)

cards.interpretation: In germline CEBPA families, N-terminal variants have higher AML penetrance than C-terminal variants.
cards.locator: Section 2.1.1 (Overview)

cards.locator: Section 2.1.1 (Overview)

cards.locator: Section 2.1.1 (Overview)

cards.interpretation: CEBPA-associated familial AML has a better prognosis than sporadic CEBPA-associated AML.
cards.locator: Section 2.1.1 (Overview)

cards.interpretation: Heterozygous germline DDX41 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to hematologic malignancy, most commonly MDS and AML.

cards.interpretation: Detection of KIT D816V or another activating KIT mutation in bone marrow, peripheral blood, or another extracutaneous organ is a minor diagnostic criterion for systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; Table 1

cards.interpretation: For systemic mastocytosis, KIT D816V variant allele fraction of at least 10% in bone marrow or peripheral-blood leukocytes is a WHO B-finding used in smoldering systemic mastocytosis classification; ICC does not use this molecular B-finding.
cards.locator: What is next after making a diagnosis of SM?

cards.interpretation: In a patient with elevated basal serum tryptase, detection of KIT D816V increases the likelihood of systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: How to diagnose SM?

cards.interpretation: When an associated hematologic neoplasm may obscure systemic mastocytosis, an NGS-detected KIT mutation should prompt bone-marrow reevaluation for occult SM-AHN.
cards.locator: How to diagnose SM?; occult SM-AHN paragraph

cards.interpretation: KIT D816V negativity alone does not exclude well-differentiated systemic mastocytosis because non-D816V KIT variants or no detectable KIT mutation can occur in this subtype.

cards.interpretation: KIT D816V negativity alone does not exclude mast-cell leukemia within systemic mastocytosis because non-D816V KIT variants or no detectable KIT mutation can occur in this subtype.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: KIT D816V negativity alone does not exclude aggressive systemic mastocytosis because non-D816V KIT variants or no detectable KIT mutation can occur in this subtype.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: In systemic mastocytosis evaluation, CD117/KIT and mast-cell tryptase identify mast cells but cannot establish a neoplastic mast-cell phenotype because they do not distinguish abnormal from normal mast cells.
cards.locator: How to diagnose SM?; bone-marrow immunophenotyping paragraph

cards.interpretation: In systemic mastocytosis evaluation, mast-cell tryptase and CD117/KIT should both be assessed because neoplastic mast cells can degranulate and show weak or absent tryptase staining while retaining strong CD117/KIT staining.
cards.locator: How to diagnose SM?; bone-marrow immunophenotyping paragraph

cards.interpretation: In an eosinophilic patient with systemic mastocytosis being evaluated for an associated hematologic neoplasm, a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine-kinase fusion must be excluded if no KIT mutation is detected.

cards.interpretation: Rare true systemic mastocytosis with an associated eosinophil neoplasm can harbor both a KIT mutation and a PDGFR rearrangement, so detection of both abnormalities does not by itself exclude coexistence of systemic mastocytosis and the eosinophil neoplasm.
cards.locator: What is next after making a diagnosis of SM?; eosinophilia/kinase-fusion paragraph

cards.interpretation: Bone-marrow immunohistochemistry for systemic mastocytosis should include mast-cell tryptase, CD117/KIT, CD2, CD25, and CD30.
cards.locator: How to diagnose SM?; bone-marrow immunophenotyping paragraph

cards.interpretation: Multilineage KIT involvement is an independent poor prognostic factor in indolent systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: In nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis, KIT variant allele fraction of at least 6% is associated with inferior overall survival compared with lower KIT variant allele fraction.
cards.locator: What is next after making a diagnosis of SM?; prognostication paragraph

cards.interpretation: In patients with systemic mastocytosis undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, absence of a KIT mutation is associated with unfavorable survival.
cards.locator: Treatment; allo-HCT paragraph

cards.interpretation: Imatinib is FDA-approved for systemic mastocytosis with wild-type KIT.
cards.locator: Treatment; KIT inhibitors paragraph

cards.interpretation: Imatinib is ineffective in KIT D816V-mutated systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: Avapritinib, a KIT D816V-selective inhibitor, is FDA-approved for advanced systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: Treatment; advanced systemic mastocytosis approvals paragraph

cards.interpretation: When systemic mastocytosis is morphologically present but standard NGS is negative for KIT, high-sensitivity KIT D816V testing with droplet-digital or allele-specific PCR capable of detecting variants below about 0.1% VAF should be performed to avoid false-negative results.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: KIT D816V is often detectable even when systemic mastocytosis is morphologically occult, supporting KIT testing as a means of uncovering otherwise hidden systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: Diagnosis and classification; KIT mutation paragraph

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, clonal haematopoiesis is recognized as a precursor myeloid disease state, and CHIP is defined as clonal haematopoiesis with somatic mutations in myeloid malignancy-associated genes detected in blood or bone marrow at VAF ≥2% (≥4% for X-linked gene mutations in males), in the absence of a diagnosed haematologic disorder or unexplained cytopenia.
cards.locator: CLONAL HAEMATOPOIESIS — CHIP definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CCUS is defined as CHIP with one or more persistent cytopenias that are otherwise unexplained and that do not meet diagnostic criteria for a defined myeloid neoplasm.
cards.locator: CLONAL HAEMATOPOIESIS — CCUS definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, cytopenia thresholds harmonized across CCUS, MDS and MDS/MPN are haemoglobin <13 g/dL in males or <12 g/dL in females, absolute neutrophil count <1.8 × 10^9/L, and platelets <150 × 10^9/L.
cards.locator: CLONAL HAEMATOPOIESIS — harmonized cytopenia thresholds

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, chronic myeloid leukaemia is defined by BCR::ABL1 resulting from t(9;22)(q34;q11).
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CML definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CML is classified into chronic and blast phases; accelerated phase is omitted. Blast phase is defined by ≥20% myeloid blasts in blood or bone marrow, extramedullary proliferation of blasts, or increased lymphoblasts in blood or marrow. The optimal lymphoblast cutoff and significance of low-level B-lymphoblasts remain uncertain.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CML phase classification

cards.interpretation: In chronic-phase CML, ABL1 kinase mutations are a source of resistance to tyrosine-kinase inhibitor therapy.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CML resistance features

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, major diagnostic criteria for polycythaemia vera include elevated haemoglobin and/or haematocrit, bone-marrow trilineage hyperplasia (panmyelosis) with pleomorphic mature megakaryocytes, and JAK2 p.V617F or a JAK2 exon 12 mutation. Measurement of increased red-cell mass with 51Cr-labelled red cells is no longer a diagnostic criterion.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — PV major diagnostic criteria

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, recognition of prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis remains necessary to distinguish it from essential thrombocythaemia, polycythaemia vera and fibrotic primary myelofibrosis.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — prefibrotic PMF distinction

cards.interpretation: In primary myelofibrosis, mutations in EZH2, IDH1, IDH2, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ASXL1 are associated with poorer prognostic risk.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — additional mutations in PMF

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, chronic neutrophilic leukaemia is a BCR::ABL1-negative MPN characterized by sustained peripheral-blood neutrophilia with WBC ≥25 × 10^9/L and ≥80% segmented neutrophils and bands, bone-marrow hypercellularity due to neutrophilic granulocyte proliferation, and hepatosplenomegaly.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CNL definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, chronic eosinophilic leukaemia is defined by sustained clonal proliferation of morphologically abnormal eosinophils and eosinophil precursors producing persistent hypereosinophilia in blood and marrow. Sustained hypereosinophilia requires ≥4 weeks; both clonality and abnormal bone-marrow morphology are required; increased blasts no longer substitute for clonality; and the former “not otherwise specified” qualifier is omitted.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CEL definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MPN-U (MPN-NOS) is reserved for cases with clinical, laboratory, morphologic and molecular features of MPN that either fail criteria for a specific MPN type or overlap distinct MPN types.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — MPN-NOS

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, JMML diagnosis integrates clinical, laboratory and molecular criteria. Updated criteria exclude KMT2A rearrangements, no longer use monosomy 7 as a cytogenetic diagnostic criterion, and emphasize molecular studies demonstrating RAS-pathway activation.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — JMML diagnostic updates

cards.interpretation: JMML initiated by somatic PTPN11 mutation is described as among the most aggressive genetic types.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — JMML genetic risk

cards.interpretation: JMML associated with germline pathogenic NF1 variants is described as among the most aggressive genetic types.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — JMML genetic risk

cards.interpretation: Some JMML cases associated with pathogenic germline CBL variants can undergo spontaneous remission.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — JMML genetic risk

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, revised minor diagnostic criteria for systemic mastocytosis include any KIT mutation causing ligand-independent activation, CD30 expression, and basal serum tryptase >20 ng/mL; the tryptase value should be adjusted in hereditary alpha-tryptasaemia.
cards.locator: MASTOCYTOSIS — systemic mastocytosis minor criteria

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, KIT p.D816V with VAF ≥10% in bone-marrow cells or peripheral-blood leukocytes qualifies as a B-finding in systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: MASTOCYTOSIS — B-finding

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, bone marrow mastocytosis is a systemic mastocytosis subtype characterized by absence of skin lesions and B-findings and basal serum tryptase <125 ng/mL.
cards.locator: MASTOCYTOSIS — bone marrow mastocytosis subtype

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, the term “myelodysplastic neoplasms,” abbreviated MDS, replaces “myelodysplastic syndromes.” MDS is defined as a clonal haematopoietic neoplasm with cytopenia(s) and morphologic dysplasia, with a recommended dysplasia threshold of ≥10% in a lineage.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — core definition and dysplasia threshold

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with low blasts and isolated 5q deletion requires <5% bone-marrow blasts and <2% peripheral-blood blasts, with 5q deletion alone or with one additional abnormality other than monosomy 7 or 7q deletion. An SF3B1 mutation or a TP53 mutation that is not multi-hit does not by itself override the MDS-5q diagnosis.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-5q Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation is a genetically defined MDS type in which 5q deletion, monosomy 7 and complex karyotype are exclusionary. Detection of ≥15% ring sideroblasts may substitute for an SF3B1 mutation; for SF3B1-wild-type cases with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, “MDS with low blasts and ring sideroblasts” is an acceptable alternative term.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-SF3B1 Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation requires <20% blasts in blood and marrow plus either ≥2 TP53 mutations or one TP53 mutation with TP53 copy-number loss or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity. Two or more TP53 mutations can generally be considered multi-hit status. MDS-biTP53 supersedes MDS-5q and MDS-SF3B1 in the WHO5 genetic hierarchy.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-biTP53 Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, clinical assessment of biallelic TP53 alteration in MDS uses sequencing covering at least TP53 exons 4–11, generally coupled with assessment of TP53 copy-number status; copy loss may also be inferred by next-generation sequencing.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — TP53 biallelic-status testing

cards.interpretation: In MDS, WHO 5th Edition 2022 notes that TP53 VAF ≥50% may be regarded as presumptive, but not definitive, evidence of trans-allelic copy loss or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity when a constitutional TP53 variant has been excluded.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — TP53 allelic-state inference

cards.interpretation: MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation is regarded as very high risk in IPSS-R.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-biTP53 risk

cards.interpretation: Published data summarized by the WHO5 paper suggest that MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation may be regarded as AML-equivalent for therapeutic considerations.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-biTP53 therapeutic equivalence

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, hypoplastic MDS is a distinct MDS type defined by bone-marrow cellularity ≤25%, adjusted for age.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — hypoplastic MDS

cards.interpretation: Patients with germline pathogenic GATA2 or DDX41 variants who have hypoplastic marrow and evolve to MDS or AML are described as not responding to immunosuppressive treatment.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — hypoplastic marrow with germline predisposition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, distinction between single-lineage and multilineage dysplasia is optional rather than disease-type defining in MDS.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — lineage dysplasia terminology

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, a 20% blast cutoff is retained to delineate MDS from AML, but most AML types with defining genetic abnormalities may be diagnosed below 20% blasts. AML with BCR::ABL1 and AML with CEBPA mutation remain exceptions requiring ≥20% blasts. When a genetically defined AML is diagnosed below 20%, morphologic and molecular findings must be correlated to establish that the defining abnormality is driving the disease.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS/AML blast boundary

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, childhood MDS with low blasts replaces the former term refractory cytopenia of childhood and is defined by <5% bone-marrow blasts and <2% peripheral-blood blasts. It comprises hypocellular and NOS subtypes, and diagnosis requires exclusion of non-neoplastic causes of cytopenia, bone-marrow failure syndromes and germline pathogenic variants.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — childhood MDS-LB exclusion prerequisite

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, childhood MDS with increased blasts is defined by 5–19% bone-marrow blasts or 2–19% peripheral-blood blasts.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — childhood MDS-IB blast criteria

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CMML requires all four prerequisite criteria: persistent absolute peripheral-blood monocytosis ≥0.5 × 10^9/L and relative monocytosis ≥10%; <20% blasts/blast equivalents in blood and marrow; absence of diagnostic criteria for CML or another MPN; and absence of a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with a tyrosine-kinase fusion. Supporting criteria are dysplasia in ≥1 myeloid lineage, with ≥10% of cells affected; an acquired clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormality; and abnormal monocyte partitioning with >94% classical monocytes in the absence of active autoimmune/systemic inflammatory disease. With monocytosis ≥1 × 10^9/L, at least one supporting criterion is required; with monocytosis ≥0.5 but <1 × 10^9/L, both dysplasia and clonality are required. A prior MPN excludes CMML; MPN-type marrow features and/or a high burden of JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations support MPN with monocytosis rather than CMML.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CMML prerequisite monocytosis

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CMML is subtyped as myelodysplastic CMML when WBC <13 × 10^9/L and myeloproliferative CMML when WBC ≥13 × 10^9/L. Blast-based subgrouping comprises CMML-1 with <5% blasts/promonocytes in blood and <10% in marrow and CMML-2 with 5–19% in blood and 10–19% in marrow; CMML-0 is no longer recognized.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CMML WBC subtypes

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, atypical chronic myeloid leukaemia is renamed MDS/MPN with neutrophilia.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — MDS/MPN with neutrophilia terminology

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis is redefined on the basis of SF3B1 mutation and renamed MDS/MPN with SF3B1 mutation and thrombocytosis. For SF3B1-wild-type cases with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis remains acceptable terminology.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — MDS/MPN-SF3B1-T

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML is organized into two families: AML with defining genetic abnormalities and AML defined by differentiation. The term AML, NOS is no longer applied to the differentiation-defined family.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — overall WHO5 grouping

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, DEK::NUP214 or RBM15::MRTFA is classified as AML with a defining genetic abnormality.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — Table 7 defining genetic abnormalities

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with BCR::ABL1 requires ≥20% blasts, principally to avoid overlap with CML.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — BCR::ABL1 blast threshold

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with CEBPA mutation includes either biallelic CEBPA mutations or a single CEBPA mutation in the basic leucine zipper region and requires ≥20% blasts.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — CEBPA blast threshold

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with KMT2A, MECOM or NUP98 rearrangement may be diagnosed with <20% blasts.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — rearrangement-defined AML

cards.interpretation: In AML, KMT2A, MECOM and NUP98 rearrangements, particularly NUP98 rearrangements, may be cryptic on conventional karyotyping.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — cryptic rearrangements

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, identification of the KMT2A fusion partner in AML with KMT2A rearrangement is desirable, although not required, because it may affect disease monitoring.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — KMT2A fusion-partner identification

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with NPM1 mutation may be diagnosed irrespective of blast count, with judicious clinicopathologic correlation.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — NPM1 definition

cards.interpretation: MDS or MDS/MPN harbouring NPM1 mutation is described as progressing to AML over a short period of time.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — NPM1 in prior MDS/MDS-MPN

cards.interpretation: Acquisition of NPM1 mutation in CHIP is similarly associated with rapid progression to AML.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acquired NPM1 in clonal haematopoiesis

cards.interpretation: In AML, a single CEBPA mutation in the basic leucine zipper region is associated with favourable prognosis in children and adults up to age 70.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — CEBPA bZIP prognosis

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, somatic RUNX1 mutation does not define a standalone AML type because it lacks sufficient specificity across defining molecular contexts.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — RUNX1 mutation classification

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML, myelodysplasia-related (AML-MR; formerly AML with myelodysplasia-related changes) requires ≥20% blasts with a myeloid immunophenotype plus at least one qualifying MDS-related feature: a history of MDS or MDS/MPN; a defining somatic mutation in ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1 or ZRSR2; or a defining cytogenetic abnormality comprising complex karyotype (≥3 abnormalities), 5q deletion/loss, monosomy 7 or 7q deletion/loss, 11q deletion, 12p deletion/loss, monosomy 13 or 13q deletion, 17p deletion/loss, isochromosome 17q or idic(X)(q13). Morphologic dysplasia alone is insufficient. A diagnosis of acute erythroid leukaemia supersedes AML-MR.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML-MR core definition

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with minimal differentiation requires blasts negative (<3%) for MPO and SBB by cytochemistry and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens such as CD13, CD33 and CD117. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML with minimal differentiation (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML without maturation requires ≥3% blasts positive for MPO or SBB, NSE negativity, <10% maturing granulocytic cells and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML without maturation (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with maturation requires ≥3% blasts positive for MPO or SBB, ≥10% maturing granulocytic cells, <20% monocyte-lineage cells and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML with maturation (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute basophilic leukaemia requires basophilic blasts/immature or mature basophils with metachromasia on toluidine blue, blasts negative for MPO, SBB and NSE, and absence of strong CD117-equivalent expression. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute basophilic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute myelomonocytic leukaemia requires ≥20% monocytes and precursors, ≥20% maturing granulocytic cells and ≥3% blasts positive for MPO. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute myelomonocytic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute monocytic leukaemia requires ≥80% monocytes and/or their precursors, <20% maturing granulocytic cells, and blasts/promonocytes expressing at least two monocytic markers among CD11c, CD14, CD36 and CD64 or showing NSE positivity. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute monocytic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute erythroid leukaemia is characterized by erythroid predominance, usually ≥80% of marrow cellularity, with ≥30% proerythroblasts; cases with <80% erythroid cellularity are recognized when they share the same clinicopathologic features. “Pure erythroid leukaemia” is retained as an acceptable related term. The other shared differentiation-defined AML exclusions apply, but the ≥20% blast requirement does not.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute erythroid leukaemia

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia requires blasts expressing at least one platelet glycoprotein marker—CD41, CD61 or CD42b. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with other defined genetic alterations provides a classification category for uncommon or emerging genetically defined AML subtypes, including rare genetic fusions; CBFA2T3::GLIS2 is recognized in this category in the acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia context.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AMKL/RAM immunophenotype

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, a myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy (MN-pCT) is diagnosed when criteria for AML, MDS or MDS/MPN are fulfilled in a patient with a documented history of chemotherapy or large-field radiation therapy for an unrelated neoplasm. CCUS is excluded. NPM1-mutated disease and core-binding-factor leukaemias with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 or CBFB::MYH11 still receive the post-cytotoxic designation when the exposure history is present. PARP1 inhibitors qualify as an exposure and methotrexate does not. The specific myeloid diagnosis should be given when possible with “post cytotoxic therapy” appended.
cards.locator: SECONDARY MYELOID NEOPLASMS — disease-attribute framework

cards.interpretation: In AML or MDS post cytotoxic therapy, biallelic/multi-hit TP53 alterations—including ≥2 TP53 mutations or a TP53 mutation with 17p/TP53 deletion or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity—are associated with worse outcomes.
cards.locator: SECONDARY MYELOID NEOPLASMS — TP53 allelic state after cytotoxic therapy

cards.interpretation: PPM1D and other DNA-damage-response mutations detected in myeloid neoplasms post cytotoxic therapy may warrant additional work-up for germline predisposition.
cards.locator: SECONDARY MYELOID NEOPLASMS — possible germline work-up

cards.interpretation: JMML can arise in association with germline pathogenic NF1 variants in neurofibromatosis type 1 or pathogenic germline CBL variants.
cards.locator: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — JMML germline genetic background

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, a germline predisposition syndrome involving myeloid neoplasms is classified by coupling the myeloid disease phenotype with the predisposing germline genotype. The framework includes: without a pre-existing platelet disorder or organ dysfunction—germline CEBPA, DDX41 or TP53 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants; with a pre-existing platelet disorder—germline RUNX1, ANKRD26 or ETV6 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants; and with potential organ dysfunction—including germline GATA2, SAMD9 or SAMD9L pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants and biallelic germline BLM pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants. SAMD9L-related ataxia-pancytopenia syndrome may occur without ataxia.
cards.locator: SECONDARY MYELOID NEOPLASMS — germline predisposition subtypes (Table 10)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, in the germline predisposition syndrome context, myeloid proliferations associated with constitutional trisomy 21 comprise transient abnormal myelopoiesis, confined to the first 6 months of life, and myeloid leukaemia of Down syndrome; these proliferations are typically associated with somatic GATA1 exon 2 or 3 mutation.
cards.locator: SECONDARY MYELOID NEOPLASMS — Down syndrome myeloid proliferations

diseases: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and TK fusion
cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) are BCR::ABL1-negative neoplasms driven by defining tyrosine-kinase rearrangements; eosinophilia is common but is not required. Defining abnormalities include rearrangements of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2 or FLT3; ETV6::ABL1; and other defined fusions including ETV6::FGFR2, ETV6::LYN, ETV6::NTRK3, RANBP2::ALK, BCR::RET and FGFR1OP::RET. MLN-TK supersedes other myeloid or lymphoid diagnoses and systemic mastocytosis in the diagnostic hierarchy, must be excluded before diagnosing CEL, and MLN-TK with ETV6::ABL1 should be distinguished from B-ALL with ETV6::ABL1.
cards.locator: MYELOID/LYMPHOID NEOPLASMS WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND TYROSINE KINASE GENE FUSIONS — diagnostic hierarchy

diseases: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and TK fusion
cards.interpretation: In myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase fusion (MLN-TK), FIP1L1::PDGFRA commonly results from a cytogenetically cryptic deletion of 4q12.
cards.locator: MYELOID/LYMPHOID NEOPLASMS WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND TYROSINE KINASE GENE FUSIONS — cryptic FIP1L1::PDGFRA

diseases: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and TK fusion
cards.interpretation: In myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase fusion (MLN-TK), PDGFRA- or PDGFRB-rearranged disease is highly sensitive to tyrosine-kinase inhibitor therapy, particularly imatinib, with major alteration of the natural history of the disease.
cards.locator: MYELOID/LYMPHOID NEOPLASMS WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND TYROSINE KINASE GENE FUSIONS — TKI sensitivity

diseases: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and TK fusion

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, polycythemia vera requires either all 3 major criteria or the first 2 major criteria plus the minor criterion. Major criteria are: elevated hemoglobin (>16.5 g/dL in men or >16.0 g/dL in women), elevated hematocrit (>49% in men or >48% in women), or red-cell mass >25% above predicted; JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation; and age-adjusted hypercellular marrow with trilineage proliferation (panmyelosis). The minor criterion is a subnormal serum erythropoietin level.
cards.locator: Myeloproliferative neoplasms; PV; Table 3

cards.interpretation: In patients with sustained absolute erythrocytosis (hemoglobin >18.5 g/dL in men or >16.5 g/dL in women and hematocrit >55.5% in men or >49.5% in women) plus JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation, a bone marrow biopsy may not be required for polycythemia vera diagnosis.
cards.locator: Myeloproliferative neoplasms; PV; Table 3

cards.interpretation: In JAK2 exon 12-mutated polycythemia vera with isolated erythrocytosis and erythroid-predominant marrow, the usual panmyelosis diagnostic criterion may not apply.

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis requires both required criteria—previous established polycythemia vera and bone-marrow fibrosis grade 2 or 3—plus at least 2 additional criteria: anemia or sustained loss of requirement for phlebotomy/cytoreductive treatment for erythrocytosis; leukoerythroblastosis; increased or newly palpable splenomegaly; or development of at least 2 of >10% weight loss in 6 months, night sweats, and unexplained fever >37.5°C.

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, essential thrombocythemia requires all 4 major criteria or the first 3 major criteria plus the minor criterion. Major criteria are platelet count >=450 x 10^9/L; characteristic megakaryocytic-lineage proliferation with enlarged mature hyperlobulated megakaryocytes and no significant granulocytic/erythroid proliferation or relevant fibrosis; exclusion of BCR::ABL1-positive CML, polycythemia vera, primary myelofibrosis, and other myeloid neoplasms; and JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutation. The minor criterion is another clonal marker or absence of reactive thrombocytosis.
cards.locator: Myeloproliferative neoplasms; essential thrombocythemia; Table 4

cards.interpretation: Small dense megakaryocyte clusters can occur infrequently in essential thrombocythemia and therefore do not by themselves exclude that diagnosis.

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis requires both required criteria—previous established essential thrombocythemia and bone-marrow fibrosis grade 2 or 3—plus at least 2 additional criteria: anemia with a >2 g/dL decrease from baseline hemoglobin; leukoerythroblastosis; increased or newly palpable splenomegaly; elevated LDH; or development of at least 2 of >10% weight loss in 6 months, night sweats, and unexplained fever >37.5°C.

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, pre-fibrotic/early primary myelofibrosis requires all 3 major criteria and at least 1 minor criterion confirmed on 2 consecutive determinations. Major criteria are characteristic megakaryocytic proliferation/atypia with marrow fibrosis <grade 2, increased age-adjusted cellularity, granulocytic proliferation and often decreased erythropoiesis; JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutation, another clonal marker, or absence of reactive reticulin fibrosis; and exclusion of BCR::ABL1-positive CML, polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, MDS, and other myeloid neoplasms. Minor criteria are unexplained anemia, leukocytosis >=11 x 10^9/L, palpable splenomegaly, or elevated LDH.

cards.interpretation: According to the ICC, overt primary myelofibrosis requires all 3 major criteria and at least 1 minor criterion confirmed on 2 consecutive determinations. Major criteria are megakaryocytic proliferation/atypia with reticulin and/or collagen fibrosis grade 2 or 3; JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutation, another clonal marker, or absence of reactive myelofibrosis; and exclusion of essential thrombocythemia, polycythemia vera, BCR::ABL1-positive CML, MDS, and other myeloid neoplasms. Minor criteria are unexplained anemia, leukocytosis >=11 x 10^9/L, palpable splenomegaly, elevated LDH, or leukoerythroblastosis.

publication_type_verdict.reason: The paper's principal contribution is original empirical data: an 81-patient cohort of older patients receiving frontline venetoclax-based combinations, with serial bulk and single-cell sequencing, RT-qPCR molecular response data, and CRISPR/Cas9 functional experiments. It presents no formal guideline methodology, no group consensus classification, and no explicit literature-search or study-selection method.

SF3B1a—SF3B1 mutation without BCOR, BCORL1, RUNX1, NRAS, STAG2, SRSF2, or del(5q)—is a main-effect finding that individually contributes favourable prognostic weight. A main-effect finding is modelled individually in IPSS-M, so its gene-specific prognostic contribution is incorporated directly rather than through the residual mutation count.
